<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-author">Author</button></h2><div id="work-acc-author" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"><div class="accordion-body"><p class="mb-0 work-author"><a href="../poets/udbhatta.html">Udbhaṭṭa</a></p></div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Udbhaṭṭa is also known for his commentary on the Nāṭya śāstra, a Sanskrit text on the performing arts written by Bharata Muni. The commentary is commonly referred to as the &quot;Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra&quot; and is considered one of the most important commentaries on the text. The Ṭīkā is written in the traditional style of Sanskrit commentaries, with Udbhaṭṭa providing detailed explanations and analysis of the various topics and concepts discussed in the Nāṭya śāstra. The commentary also includes a number of examples and illustrations to help clarify the text. The Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra is a valuable resource for scholars and students of Indian classical dance, music, and theatre.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra by Udbhaṭṭa is a commentary on the Nāṭya śāstra, which is an ancient Indian text on performing arts attributed to the sage Bharata. The commentary by Udbhaṭṭa includes detailed explanations and interpretations of the concepts and techniques described in the Nāṭya śāstra, including the types of plays, the stage, the characters, the costumes, the makeup, the music, the dance, and the emotions. Udbhaṭṭa also provides examples from various sources to illustrate the principles and practices of the Nāṭya śāstra, and offers his own insights and critiques of the text. The commentary is divided into chapters or Adhyāyas, each focusing on a particular aspect of the Nāṭya śāstra, and is written in Sanskrit.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra by Udbhaṭṭa is a significant commentary on the ancient Indian text of dramatic theory and performance, the Nāṭya śāstra. What sets Udbhaṭṭa's Ṭīkā apart from other commentaries is its comprehensive nature and its attention to detail. Udbhaṭṭa meticulously explains various aspects of the Nāṭya śāstra such as its history, its philosophical underpinnings, and its practical applications in theatrical performances. He also draws on a wide range of sources to support his interpretations, including other commentaries, ancient scriptures, and contemporary theatrical practices. Overall, Udbhaṭṭa's Ṭīkā provides a valuable and unique perspective on the Nāṭya śāstra that is still studied and referenced by scholars and practitioners of Indian theatre and performance today.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra by Udbhaṭṭa is a significant commentary on the ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, the Nāṭya śāstra. The commentary provides a detailed explanation of the concepts and techniques outlined in the Nāṭya śāstra and offers valuable insights into the aesthetics of Indian theatre, dance, and music. The work contributed to the development of Indian performing arts and helped to preserve and transmit the knowledge and techniques of the Nāṭya śāstra to future generations. Its influence can be seen in the many later works on Indian performing arts that drew on its insights and ideas.<br><br>The Ṭīkā on Nāṭya śāstra by Udbhaṭṭa is considered to be one of the most important commentaries on the Nāṭya śāstra. It provides a detailed and comprehensive explanation of the text and is often cited by scholars as a primary source for understanding the Sanskrit dramatic tradition. Additionally, Udbhaṭṭa's commentary includes many references to other works on drama and aesthetics, providing valuable insights into the wider literary and cultural context of the Nāṭya śāstra.</div></div></div>
